static_traits.name: Lin Ke
static_traits.family_status: Has two children with his wife
static_traits.social_status: Having a supportive wife to discuss feelings with
static_traits.medical_history: Never had similar psychological issues; never received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Expresses himself clearly with fairly coherent logic, a neutral tone, and good cooperation; can describe guilt and the sense of losing contact in concrete terms

basic_info.main_problem: Due to long-term on-the-road work, feeling distant from the children and not recognized by them, triggering persistent guilt and a sense of disconnection, and affecting leisure and family relationships.
basic_info.core_demands: Hopes to reduce guilt and be more connected with the child; seeks a professional perspective to understand and improve the parent-child estrangement caused by work arrangements.
growth_experiences: About a year ago work hours increased and time with family clearly decreased; guilt and disconnection recur with every driving trip; stress was moderate at first but gradually escalated as work kept being placed above family time; tried compensating by bringing gifts home and arranging special outings, but the guilt has not yet eased; this state affects leisure (e.g. unable to enjoy playing baseball) and the relationship with the wife (starting to feel tense). The client has not yet talked with the children about these feelings, worrying about burdening them.

special_situations.event: Driving long hours on the road, thinking of the children growing up without my company
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot stay present consistently, it means I am an unqualified parent, and the children will not know me either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to make up for absence by bringing gifts home and arranging special outings
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My children do not know me at all; they will grow up without me

special_situations.event: After returning from working away, has positive interactions with the children (such as family picnics and helping his son with a science project)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only continuous, high-frequency company counts as real parent-child connection; scattered good moments 'do not count'
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring positive evidence, continues arranging more activities to prove oneself a good parent
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These good moments are not enough, do not count, I have not done enough

special_situations.event: Notices the relationship with his wife becoming tense; worries that absence disappoints the family
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Family members' feelings and relationships being affected is my fault; the responsibility is all mine
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Blames herself and avoids talking with the child about her emotions so as not to 'add burden'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault,I let them down

special_situations.event: Reviews the past year's increased work hours and decreased companionship
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A period of absence equals completely losing the parent-child connection
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Evaluates parent-child relationship success by global, absolute standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not know me; I am just someone who shows up occasionally

core_conflict.wish: Longing to build a stable, intimate connection with one's children and be recognized as an important father figure
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being treated as a stranger by the children due to work absence, not being needed, and eventually being rejected or losing the sense of worth of the father identity
defense_goal: Avoids expressing vulnerability to the children to avoid adding burden; uses compensatory actions (giving gifts, arranging activities) to maintain a sense of connection and avoid direct communication

object_relations.self_representation: A guilty, absent father, worried about not being recognized and accepted
object_relations.object_representation: Children represented as possibly-estranged onlookers unfamiliar with oneself; the wife as supportive but someone one may disappoint

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether they have talked with the child about their feelings, or when thinking about communicating directly with the child
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Expressing inner feelings would burden the children and make them uncomfortable (worrying about being misunderstood or rejected)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing in a gentle, restrained tone 'the children are still young, I do not want to burden them', steering the topic toward work arrangements or compensation plans, avoiding deep feelings and needs.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: On the road or when thinking about guilt from being absent
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes one has hurt the children and needs to make up for the fault through behavior
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'bringing gifts, arranging special outings' as ways to make up, downplaying the possibility of direct heart-to-heart talks or steady daily company, tone self-blaming but avoiding vulnerable expression.

manifestations: Working on the road long-term, less time with family
Worrying the children do not know oneself or only see oneself as someone who shows up occasionally
Avoids talking with the children about one's emotions so as not to 'add burden'
outcomes: Persistent guilt and sense of disconnection
Hard to enjoy leisure activities (e.g. playing baseball)
Tension arising in the relationship with wife

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains impulses to act toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, turning libidinal energy meant for outward release back onto the self.
manifestations: Knowingly disconnected yet not talking feelings with the children, choosing to 'bear it', digesting inner impulses through self-blame and compensatory behaviors instead

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-blame ('It is all my fault'), believing good moments are 'not enough', cautious about parent-child interaction, repressing the impulse for direct connection for fear of burdening the children

exception_events.target_problem: While driving on trips, the client usually feels strong guilt and disconnection, believing the children do not know them, thus reducing active connection.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At last month's family picnic, the client laughed and interacted with the children and wife, subjectively experienced a strong sense of connection and felt he was a part of their lives.
exception_events.reason: Different situation: at home doing activities with family, not on the road; different action: actively participating in family activities; different support: wife and children present, interactions natural, enhancing the connection experience.

exception_events.target_problem: When thinking about communicating feelings with the child, the client usually avoids the conversation, worrying about adding burden to the child, and the parent-child relationship thus remains in an alienated state.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On an occasion helping their son with a science project, the client devoted companionship and practical support; the child appeared very happy, and the client at the moment felt needed and recognized.
exception_events.reason: Different action: focusing interaction on concrete tasks and support, lowering the pressure of emotional expression; different situation: at home with clear tasks; the children's positive feedback reinforced the sense of connection.

positive_force: Having a supportive wife and family atmosphere
Can proactively create concrete moments of connection (family picnics, helping with schoolwork)
Good work performance, possessing a sense of responsibility
negative_force: Catastrophizing and overgeneralizing cognitive patterns reinforce the sense of disconnection
Self-denial and persistent guilt, tending to attribute all responsibility to oneself
Long hours on the road reduce real companionship
Avoids direct communication with the children so as not to 'add burden'

target_behavior.behavior: Strong guilt and disconnection while driving on trips, repeatedly thinking 'the children do not know me'
antecedent: Working on the road for long periods
Thinking of being absent from important moments in the children's growth
Reviews and compares the increase in work hours over the past year
target_behavior.core_reason: Directly equating absence with 'incompetent parent', with catastrophizing, overgeneralizing and personalizing cognitive biases, reinforcing negative emotions and self-blame.
target_behavior.function: Escaping the anxiety of parent-child communication and possible rejection, maintaining a 'sense of control' over the relationship and compensation motivation through self-blame (briefly reducing uncertainty).
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent guilt and sense of disconnection, difficulty enjoying leisure activities, relationship tension with the wife.

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids talking with the children about his own feelings and inner needs
antecedent: When asked whether one communicates with the children
When thinking about expressing feelings directly to the children
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about burdening the children, fearing that exposed vulnerability will be misunderstood or rejected, tending to rationalize avoidant behavior.
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome emotions and possible uncomfortable interactions (briefly reducing anxiety).
target_behavior.consequence: The parent-child relationship stays distant, guilt cannot be eased, and the sense of connection is hard to consolidate.
